minutes.headline: Planning Board continued the Powell gravel site plan to February and voted to waive first refusal on Northfield Road land.
minutes.summary: The board approved a lot-line swap and a minor change at Asian Imperial, then heard a long Powell stone and gravel site plan hearing that was continued pending Conservation review and a possible zone-line change. It spent much time on draft cannabis cultivation rules, voted to send questions to the Cannabis Control Commission, endorsed the open space plan, and argued over who leads a master plan. It ended by going into executive session on litigation.

attendees.role: presenter, principal planner, regional planning commission

public_comment.topic: A speaker raised the Planning Board's silence on reuse of vacant municipal buildings; discussion followed on economic development and the master plan.
A speaker noted the Lunenburg Grange is being rechartered and the 300th anniversary of settlement in December 2018.

Accept the Asian Imperial de minimis change with a note documenting seats and required parking.
Accept the waivers as documented for the Powell hearing.

Draft a letter to the Cannabis Control Commission with the board's questions.
Send a letter of support for the open space plan.
Recommend the selectmen waive their right of first refusal on the Northfield Road parcel.
Enter executive session to discuss litigation strategy (O'Brien Homes cases), not to return to regular session.

Master plan discussion with the town manager deferred to the January 14 meeting; board chose not to discuss it without it being on the agenda.
Planning staff will draft the CCC letter, send questions to town counsel separately.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the Powell stone and gravel site plan hearing to its February meeting after voting to accept the waivers as documented.
The board voted to recommend the selectmen waive their right of first refusal on the Northfield Road parcel.
After long discussion of draft cannabis cultivation rules, the board voted to draft a letter to the Cannabis Control Commission with its questions.
The board voted to send a letter of support for the open space plan; a master plan talk with the town manager was deferred to January 14.
The board accepted the Chase Road lot-line swap plan and the Asian Imperial minor change, with a note documenting seats and required parking.

why_it_matters: The first-refusal recommendation bears on whether the town budget, mostly taxes, takes on a land purchase, and an independent appraisal was said to cost in the tens of thousands.

The Powell gravel hearing and the cannabis cultivation rules decide what may be built or grown near neighbors and conservation land, and a master plan consultant would be a future capital request competing with requests that far exceed available funds.
watch_next: Powell site plan hearing resumes at the February meeting, pending Conservation review and a possible zone-line change.
Master plan discussion with the town manager is set for the January 14 meeting.
